intervals.quote: the detector performance achieved during its commissioning with a mini-CryoCube module consisting of three 42-gram germanium cryogenic calorimeters

name: Ricochet CryoCube (Ge/Zn cryogenic calorimeter array)
notes: Two mass figures from two different papers/phases: the full, final CryoCube is described only qualitatively as a 'kg-scale' Ge+Zn array (arXiv:2208.01760, a background-characterization paper for the planned final detector); the commissioning-phase mini-CryoCube module actually operated and characterized (arXiv:2507.22751) is precisely 3 x 42 g = 126 g of germanium. specs.target_mass below records the precisely-quoted mini-CryoCube figure.

placements.quote: a research nuclear reactor operated by the Institut Laue-Langevin (Grenoble, France)

target_mass.display: 126 g (3 x 42 g Ge, mini-CryoCube commissioning module)
target_mass.note: 126 g is derived as 3 x 42 g from the quoted three 42-gram germanium cryogenic calorimeters (the source does not state the total). This is the commissioning-phase mini-CryoCube module actually characterized; the planned full CryoCube is described only qualitatively as 'kg-scale' combining Ge and Zn crystals (arXiv:2208.01760), with no precise total mass quoted in a source cited here.

summary.plain: A set of ultra-cold germanium and zinc crystals, weighing from a few dozen grams (in the test module now running) up to a planned kilogram scale, designed to catch reactor antineutrinos nudging whole atomic nuclei.
summary.technical: Ricochet CryoCube: planned kg-scale array of Ge and Zn cryogenic calorimeters; a mini-CryoCube commissioning module of three 42 g germanium calorimeters (126 g total) achieved 40 eV ionization / 50-80 eV phonon baseline resolutions during 2025 commissioning at the ILL.

technology.quote: kg-scale low-energy-threshold detector array combining Ge and Zn target crystals
technology.value: cryogenic heat-and-ionization germanium and zinc calorimeters (CryoCube)
